summary: The three flags transcendence row 9 approved — `fca [--entity cppag|ke] [--cumulative] [--billing-month 2020-01]` — are hand-authored and attached by AUGMENTING the generated `fca` command in place from a novel hook. The shipped command had no flags at all.
reason: Two things made this necessary. (1) THE FLAGS WERE NEVER BUILT. The Phase 3 completion gate is STRUCTURAL — it resolves a command PATH — so `fca` passed it while carrying none of the three approved flags; verify-skill and the Sample Output Probe both caught it (`unknown flag: --entity`). (2) THE COMMAND CANNOT BE REPLACED, ONLY AUGMENTED. internal/cli/promoted_fca.go carries a DO NOT EDIT header, and its command is not a novel scaffold, so addNovelCommandIfAbsent returns early on the name collision and cannot substitute a hand-authored replacement. The hook therefore calls root.Find(["fca"]), adds the flags to the existing *cobra.Command and wraps its RunE, preserving the generated Short, Example, annotations and fetch path. With no flag given the captured generated RunE runs unchanged, so default output is byte-identical to before the patch (verified). THE DATA HAZARD IS THE ACCOUNTING NEGATIVE: this sheet writes negatives in parentheses — "(2.5935)" — and there are 49 such cells across the 48 published rows. strconv.ParseFloat REJECTS that string, so code that ignores the error reads a real negative tariff adjustment as ZERO, and code that strips the parentheses without restoring the sign reads it as POSITIVE. Both silently reverse the direction of an adjustment. An EMPTY cell is a third case and is absence, not zero: with one side absent neither the disallowance nor the allowed-below-requested comparison is computed at all, because an arithmetic against a missing operand is an invention.
reapply_after_regen: internal/cli/nepra_fca_series{,_test}.go are markerless hand-authored files and survive regeneration. TWO EDITS TO THE GENERATED internal/cli/promoted_fca.go MUST BE RE-APPLIED, and this file already carries a third from nepra-html-table-extraction: (a) the three flag declarations near the end of newFcaPromotedCmd, and (b) the four-line branch at the TOP of RunE that calls fcaFilteredSeries(cmd, flags) and returns when it reports handled. Without (b) the flags parse and are then ignored — the command accepts --entity and returns the unfiltered sheet, which is silent. USE THE XxxVar FORMS FOR (a): cmd.Flags().StringVar(&local, "entity", ...) is recognised by verify-skill's flag scanner while the otherwise-identical cmd.Flags().String("entity", ...) is reported as "--entity is not declared in any internal/cli/*.go". The flags are declared in the GENERATED file rather than the hand-authored sibling on purpose: verify-skill attributes a flag to a command by finding the declaration alongside that command's own Use: literal, and declaring them elsewhere produced the false finding "--entity is declared elsewhere but not on fca" about a flag that worked. VERIFY WITH DATA, NOT A GREP: `fca --entity cppag --cumulative --json` must report cumulative_disallowance EXACTLY 8.8425, not 8.842499999999998.
validated_outcome: The shipped command reproduces the absorb manifest's headline exactly — the figure the manifest records as never having been computed by anyone: CPPA-G cumulative requested 81.9748, allowed 73.1323, disallowance 8.8425 Rs/kWh, allowed below requested in 45 of 48 months, over 48 distinct year-months Jul 2018..Jun 2022 with no gap and no duplicate. K-Electric carries 19 months with a negative figure, each summed with its sign. Exit codes: 0 success, 2 an unknown --entity or a malformed --billing-month, 3 a well-formed billing month this sheet does not publish (unpublished and empty are different findings). With no flag the output is byte-identical to the generated command's. A FLOAT-DUST DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED HERE, and how it hid is the lesson: the first build emitted cumulative_disallowance 8.842499999999998 and a monthly 0.37749999999999995, because float64 cannot represent the published operands and 48 accumulated differences drift. A test that printed the value with %.4f PASSED against that build - the dust is invisible to formatted output and only appears in the raw JSON number, which is what a consumer parses. Derived values are now snapped to the source's own published precision (four decimals, measured, and pinned to that measurement by a test); a published operand is never touched. The regression test ALSO had to be fixed twice, both times found by mutation: Go evaluates untyped constant arithmetic at arbitrary precision, so `fcaRound(1.4883 - 1.1108)` written with literals folds to exactly 0.3775 at compile time and never sees the dust (the operands must be float64 variables); and an end-to-end check of the form `x != fcaRound(x)` is tautological whenever fcaRound is the identity, which is exactly the regression it was meant to catch. MUTATION-VERIFIED 13/13: dropping the sign, treating a parenthesised cell as positive, swallowing an unparseable cell as 0, reading an empty cell as a measured 0, computing a disallowance against a missing operand, rendering an unmeasured cumulative as 0, tidying the verbatim column headers, keeping an unknown month spelling, and summing both entities into one row are each killed by a test. The four rounding mutations are included: 2dp, 6dp, truncation instead of rounding, and an identity fcaRound. The 6dp mutation is benign on this corpus - the dust is ~1e-16 so both precisions snap identically - and is killed instead by a test that pins fcaPublishedDecimals to the maximum decimal count actually observed in the sheet, which is the real contract: rounding coarser than the source discards published detail, finer leaves dust.
upstream_issue: TO FILE - the Phase 3 completion gate resolves a manifest row's command PATH but never checks the FLAGS the same row approves. Both fca (3 flags) and licence (3 flags) passed the gate with zero of their approved flags built.
